rationale.conceptual: Using a standard equilibrium solver with public thermochemical data is a textbook implementation. There is minor customisation (two cases, suppressed phase) but no novel method or deep domain reasoning beyond what Cantera handles automatically.
rationale.execution: A single step: set up a Cantera model with the desired species, run equilibrium at a grid of temperatures, and write a CSV. No complex orchestration, external tools, or multi-stage dependency, but the species list assembly from JANAF requires some careful manual mapping.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires computing thermodynamic equilibrium compositions of a multicomponent system using standard JANAF data and a Gibbs energy minimizer (e.g., Cantera). It involves no novel algorithms, only configuration; the pipeline is a single computation step producing one CSV. Resource needs are negligible.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The equilibrium solver works on a tiny gas/solid system; JANAF data is a small text file (few MB). CPU-only trivial runtime.
